title: Fuzzy user-interest drift detection based recommender systems
research_question: Can fuzzy modeling of individual user-interest consistency combined with concept-drift detection improve recommendation accuracy when user interests evolve and item-interest information is incomplete or vague?
methodology: The authors construct a fuzzy user-interest consistency model using fuzzy-set theory and develop a user-interest drift-detection mechanism based on concept-drift techniques. Detected drift is used to guide recommendation generation so the recommender can adapt as individual interests change. The approach is evaluated empirically on synthetic data and a real-world MovieLens dataset. The accessible abstract reports recommendation performance using mean absolute error.

key_findings.finding: The paper treats user interests as time-varying rather than stationary and argues that ignoring such drift degrades recommendation accuracy.
Interest drift is modeled separately for individual users because users may change preferences in different directions.
Fuzzy-set modeling is used to address incomplete and vague representations of item features and user interests.
A drift-detection mechanism based on concept-drift methods is integrated with recommendation generation rather than relying on a static interest model.
Experiments on synthetic and MovieLens data report improved recommendation performance for the proposed approach according to mean absolute error.

limitations: Only the abstract was accessible, so the numerical MAE improvements, baselines, statistical significance, parameter settings, and detailed experimental protocol could not be verified.
The accessible abstract does not identify the exact MovieLens version or provide enough information to reconstruct the synthetic-data generator.
The work addresses preference drift in recommendation rather than explicit work-item lifecycle states such as resolved or superseded.
No evidence available in the accessible abstract addresses obligation-versus-preference prioritization.
No evidence available in the accessible abstract addresses omission, repetition, semantic supersession, or multi-thread workplace briefing.
raw_claims: The recommender models user interests as quantities that can drift over time.
Different users may experience interest drift in different directions.
Incomplete and vague item or interest information makes adaptation more difficult.
The proposed method builds a fuzzy user-interest consistency model.
Concept-drift techniques are used to detect changes in user interests.
Detected interest changes influence subsequent recommendation generation.
The approach is tested on both synthetic and real-world data.
MovieLens is used as the real-world recommendation dataset.
Mean absolute error is the reported prediction-quality metric.
The abstract reports that the proposed method improves recommendation performance in MAE.
